# fast_rspec

> Target: a Ruby gem where one Gemfile line replaces the whole test stack. Planned lean, API-compatible reimplementations of RSpec (core, expectations, mocks, rails) and Minitest (5 + 6, incl. Rails' `ActiveSupport::TestCase`), parallel on every CPU core by default, with WebMock, VCR, Faker, database cleaning, SimpleCov and (later) FactoryBot rebuilt in and auto-configured; shoulda-matchers and Capybara/Cuprite stay upstream and are auto-wired. Design constraint: zero runtime dependencies. Aimed at Rails and plain Ruby; CRuby (fork pool + C extension), JRuby and TruffleRuby (thread pool + pure-Ruby twin). No speed claim until numbers exist in `docs/benchmarks.md`.

**Status (2026-10-31): design phase — nothing below works yet.** This file describes the target contract so agents write compatible code from day one. Each section says which roadmap milestone ships it (`docs/idea/11-roadmap.md`).

Install: `gem 'fast_rspec'` in the `:development, :test` group. Remove the gems it replaces. MIT. Source: https://github.com/developerz-ai/fast_rspec. Maintained by developerz.ai (AI maintainer agent: triage, review, merges, releases).

## Rules for agents writing tests in a fast_rspec project (target)

These rules apply once the milestones below ship (M1–M7, `docs/idea/11-roadmap.md`); today only the scaffold exists.

1. Write normal RSpec or Minitest. Same DSL, matchers, assertions, hooks, CLI flags, exit codes, output. Never `require` anything fast_rspec-specific in a spec/test.
2. Don't add `rspec-*`, `minitest-reporters`, `parallel_tests`, `webmock`, `vcr`, `faker`, `database_cleaner*` or `simplecov` to the Gemfile — they are meant to be built in (M1–M6). Keep `shoulda-matchers`, `capybara`, `cuprite` if you use them; fast_rspec is planned to configure them (M5).
3. Don't write `test/support` / `spec/support` boilerplate for: FactoryBot syntax methods, WebMock `disable_net_connect!`, VCR cassette dir, shoulda `integrate`, Devise test helpers, time helpers, `parallelize(workers: :number_of_processors)`. It is planned to be automatic (M4–M6). If you do write it, yours wins.
4. Planned (M1, isolation M3): tests run on all cores, each worker with its own DB, Redis DB, tmp dir and ports. Don't share state through files, class variables or ENV between tests. Fork-safety is meant to be ours; order-independence is yours.
5. Planned: reproduce a failure with the one-line command fast_rspec will print (seed + that worker's files).

## Commands (target)

The commands below are the target contract. Today only the scaffold exists; `FAST_RSPEC_WORKERS`, `FAST_RSPEC_POOL` and `FAST_RSPEC_DISABLE_EXT` are the only env knobs read by `lib/`.

| Do | Command | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| Run everything (RSpec + Minitest) on all cores | `bundle exec fast_rspec` | M1-M2 |
| RSpec | `bundle exec rspec`, `rspec spec/x_spec.rb:12`, every upstream flag | M2 |
| Minitest / Rails | `bin/rails test`, `bin/rails test test/x_test.rb:12`, `rake test` | M1, M3 |
| Serial | `-n 1` or `FAST_RSPEC_WORKERS=1` | M1 |
| Fewer workers | `FAST_RSPEC_WORKERS=4` | M1 |
| Pool | `FAST_RSPEC_POOL=fork\|thread` (default: fork on CRuby, thread on JRuby/TruffleRuby); a `spawn` value is planned for M7 | M1, M7 |
| Force pure-Ruby twin | `FAST_RSPEC_DISABLE_EXT=1` | exists in scaffold |

## Configuration (optional, target)

```ruby
# spec/spec_helper.rb or test/test_helper.rb — only if you need to change a default
FastRspec.configure do |c|
  c.workers = 8
  c.batteries.disable :vcr, :capybara
end
```

## Batteries (target)

| Battery | API | Milestone | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| RSpec | rspec-core / -expectations / -mocks / -rails 3.13 | M2–M3 | `.rspec` honored; rails type inference |
| Minitest | minitest 5.2x + 6.x, `ActiveSupport::TestCase` | M1, M3 | `parallelize` routed to the pool |
| WebMock | webmock 3.x | M4 | `disable_net_connect!(allow_localhost: true)`, reset per test |
| VCR | vcr 6.x | M4 | only if the app already uses cassettes; atomic cassette writes |
| Faker | faker 3.x | M4 | deterministic per seed + worker; data loaded lazily |
| DB cleaning | database_cleaner 2.x | M3 | transactional tests; per-worker DB cloned from a template |
| SimpleCov | simplecov 0.22 | M5 | starts before app code; results merged across workers |
| FactoryBot | factory_bot 6.x | M6 (upstream wired until then) | definitions found, syntax methods included |
| shoulda / Capybara / Cuprite / Devise / Sidekiq | upstream gems | M5 | auto-wired: integrate, ports, browsers, helpers, fake queues |

## Pitfalls (target)

- `parallelize(workers: 1)` or `-n 1` disables parallelism; a hard-coded worker count in `test_helper.rb` is honored.
- Tests that depend on run order fail under any seed; fast_rspec just exposes them faster. Use the printed one-line repro command (planned).
- JRuby/TruffleRuby thread pool: the plan is that tests stubbing process-global state (`stub_const`, `allow_any_instance_of`, `$stdout` swaps) are routed to a separate process automatically (M7).
- Upstream behavior differences, if any, are listed in `docs/idea/parity-divergences.md`. Report others as a "Compatibility gap" issue.
